item.title: Vucic resigns as president of Serbia
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
Serbian president Aleksandar Vucic speaks during a press conference in Belgrade, Serbia, Sept. 27, 2026. Aleksandar Vucic signed and submitted his resignation on Sunday, stepping down as president. (Photo by Predrag Milosavljevic/Xinhua) BELGRADE, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic signed and submitted his resignation on Sunday, stepping down as president. "I am now signing the text that reads as follows: 'Pursuant to Article 116, paragraph 5 of the Constitution of the Republic of Serbia, I submit my resignation from the office of President of the Republic.'...Ana, this goes to the Parliament, and tomorrow you go to the handover," said Vucic. Under Serbia's Constitution and Law on the president, the president's term ends when the written resignation is formally received by the National Assembly, without requiring approval. The Speaker of the National Assembly Ana Brnabic then assumes presidential duties for up to three months and must call a presidential election within that period. Vucic also said he would take part in the snap parliamentary elections scheduled on Oct. 25 as an ordinary citizen. The Serbian parliament was dissolved on Sept. 9. Under the Constitution, a dissolved parliament has limited powers, while the government continues to perform its duties until a new government is formed. On Sept. 5, the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) nominated Vucic as head of its electoral list and its candidate for prime minister in the upcoming snap parliamentary elections. Following the Oct. 25 elections, the process of forming a new government will begin. The acting president, after consulting representatives of the elected electoral lists, proposes a prime minister candidate to the National Assembly. The candidate then presents the government's program and cabinet members, which must be approved by a majority of all lawmakers. Vucic, born in Belgrade in 1970, had served as defense minister, first deputy prime minister and prime minister. He was elected president in 2017 and re-elected in 2022. Under the Constitution, the presidential term is five years, with a maximum of two terms for any individual. ■ Serbian president Aleksandar Vucic attends a press conference in Belgrade, Serbia, Sept. 27, 2026. Aleksandar Vucic signed and submitted his resignation on Sunday, stepping down as president. (Photo by Predrag Milosavljevic/Xinhua) Serbian president Aleksandar Vucic speaks during a press conference in Belgrade, Serbia, Sept. 27, 2026. Aleksandar Vucic signed and submitted his resignation on Sunday, stepping down as president. (Photo by Predrag Milosavljevic/Xinhua)

item.title: China takes three golds as Boonson ties Asian 200m record
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- Thailand's Puripol Boonson tied the Asian record of 19.88 seconds in the men's 200m, while China claimed three athletics gold medals at the 2026 Asian Games on Sunday in the men's 110m hurdles, women's long jump and women's javelin. Chen Yuanjiang started China's run of victories by winning the men's 110m hurdles in 13.15 seconds. Japan's Rachid Muratake took silver, while the Philippines' John Tolentino claimed bronze. China had won the event at 10 consecutive Asian Games before that streak ended at the 2023 edition in Hangzhou. "I'm thrilled. We've taken this gold medal back," said Chen, who shouted, "Who's No. 1? I am!" as he crossed the finish line. In the women's javelin, Asian record holder Yan Ziyi needed just one throw to secure gold, launching the javelin 70.46 meters on her opening attempt. Olympic champion Haruka Kitaguchi of Japan took silver with 62.70 meters. Yan's mark also broke the Asian Games record of 66.09 meters set by compatriot and Olympic medalist Liu Shiying. "I didn't expect to wrap it up in one throw. My plan was actually to take it through my first two attempts, but the first one just came out well," said Yan, who had tears in her eyes after the competition. "I'm thrilled, and I can't wait to hear the anthem play," she said. Asked to compare herself with Chinese shot put great Gong Lijiao, Yan played down the comparison. "I don't think I can compare myself to her. She's a role model for me. I still have to keep learning from her and chasing what she's achieved." Looking ahead to next year's world championships in Beijing and the Olympics the following year, Yan said: "I'll keep working with my coach, and I'm hoping for the top spot." "I plan to save the new record for the world championships in Beijing, so stay tuned for that," she added. In the women's 200m, Singapore's Shanti Pereira clocked a season-best 22.78 seconds to retain her Asian Games title, while China's 17-year-old Chen Yujie, who won the 100m in a Games record, took silver in 22.93. Chen called Pereira "a rival worth respecting." "I planned to stay with her through the bend and then look for a chance to pass on the straight, but I'd used up too much energy in the first half," she said. Asked about returning to high school after the Games, Chen said her parents and those around her had given her nothing but support. "They've told me not to worry about the pressure from the internet. They never set winning gold as some hard target for me; they just want me to give it everything I've got while staying healthy." Boonson equaled the Asian record set by China's Xie Zhenye in 2019 with his 19.88-second run in the men's 200m final. China's 21-year-old Huang Youwen took silver in 20.45. "It was the first time I'd ever raced someone at that level, and it was a great experience. I'd never felt a gap that big before," Huang said. "We were only 50 meters in, and I could already tell how fast he was. He's just really, really fast." Looking ahead to next year's world championships, Huang added: "When you're young, you should dream big - set your sights on the result first, and figure out how to get there later." In the women's long jump, China's Huang Yingying came from behind with a sixth-round leap of 6.55 meters to edge India's Ancy Sojan Edappilly by two centimeters for gold. Huang's compatriot Tan Mengyi took bronze with 6.46 meters. Huang said she was far from satisfied with her performance and acknowledged that the outcome had depended on her rival's final attempts. "Having the gold come down to whether your opponent slips up is a really nerve-wracking way to win," she said. "I need to build up my own strength, so I have more of a safety net mentally." Huang also competed in Thursday's triple jump, taking silver. "My main focus is still triple jump training. Doubling up in the long jump is really just for the Asian stage," she said. "I'm hoping for a better showing on a bigger stage next year at the world championships in Beijing, and at the Olympics the year after, if I can qualify." In the men's high jump, Chinese Taipei's Fu Chao-hsuan cleared 2.25 meters to beat India's Sarvesh Kushare for gold. Qatar's 35-year-old Olympic medalist Mutaz Barshim withdrew from the final. Earlier Sunday, Japan's Hayato Katsuki clocked 3:03:36 to beat China's Zhou Yingcheng for the men's marathon race walk title, while Kazakhstan's Yasmina Toxanbayeva won the women's race in 3:22:20. China's Danzengquzong and Ma Li took silver and bronze, respectively, in the women's event. The first round of the 4x100m relays was also held Sunday, with China's men's and women's teams both winning their heats to advance to the finals. ■

item.title: China retains top spot in gold medal tally at 48th WorldSkills Competition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
SHANGHAI, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- China topped the gold medal tally at the 48th WorldSkills Competition as the event concluded in Shanghai on Sunday night, marking the fifth consecutive edition in which the country has taken the top spot. Chen Jining, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and secretary of the CPC Shanghai Municipal Committee, and Chinese State Councilor Shen Yiqin attended the closing ceremony. China's He Xiaoman received the prestigious Albert Vidal Award for her performance in the rail vehicle technology competition. The award is WorldSkills' highest honor and is presented to the competitor with the highest overall score across all skills. China competed in all 64 skills, winning 41 gold medals, 11 silver medals, four bronze medals, and six Medals for Excellence. The Chinese delegation ranked first in the gold medal tally, the overall medal tally, and the total group points standings, marking China's best-ever performance at the WorldSkills Competition. At the closing ceremony, the WorldSkills flag was officially passed to Japan's Aichi, which will host the 49th edition of the competition in 2028. The WorldSkills Competition, held every two years, is widely regarded as the world's leading vocational skills competition. This year's event, held from Sept. 22 to 27, drew 1,385 participants from 68 countries and regions. China sent 71 competitors to take part in all 64 skills at this year's competition, covering six sectors, namely transportation and logistics, construction and building technology, manufacturing and engineering technology, information and communication technology, creative arts and fashion, and social and personal services. Seven skills made their debut at this year's competition, including rail vehicle technology, unmanned aerial systems and software testing, reflecting emerging industry trends and evolving demand for vocational skills. Organized by WorldSkills International, the event was co-hosted by China's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the Shanghai municipal government. The WorldSkills Conference 2026 and WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 Expo were held alongside the competition. ■

item.title: Pair of Chinese giant pandas arrives in U.S. city Atlanta
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
A chartered FedEx cargo plane carrying a pair of Chinese giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, lands at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, in Atlanta, the United States, Sept. 27, 2026 The two giant pandas are expected to stay at Zoo Atlanta for 10 years, according to an agreement between Zoo Atlanta and the China Wildlife Conservation Association. (Zoo Atlanta/Handout via Xinhua) ATLANTA, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- A chartered FedEx cargo plane carrying a pair of Chinese giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, landed in Atlanta in the southeastern United States on Sunday morning. The pair then arrived at Zoo Atlanta and will be housed in a biosecure area of Zoo Atlanta's new giant panda complex for a routine quarantine period of around a month, according to a release by Zoo Atlanta. "This is a thrilling day for Zoo Atlanta and a historic moment for the City of Atlanta, the state of Georgia, and beyond," said Raymond B. King, president and CEO of Zoo Atlanta. "We are elated to welcome Ping Ping and Fu Shuang and could not be more excited about sharing that joy with our members, guests, city, and community in the coming weeks. Zoo Atlanta is honored to partner with the China Wildlife Conservation Association to see important work continue toward the conservation of giant pandas, which is the most important benefit of guarding this species," King added. Zoo Atlanta is now one of three zoos in the United States to house giant pandas and is the only zoological organization in the Southeast the species will call home, said the release. The two giant pandas are expected to stay at Zoo Atlanta for 10 years, according to an agreement between Zoo Atlanta and the China Wildlife Conservation Association. Chinese veterinarians and caretakers have arrived in Atlanta in advance to prepare for the pandas' arrival and support their life in quarantine, training and adjustment to the new environment, Xinhua learnt. Gina Ferrie, vice president of collections and conservation, Zoo Atlanta, said on Thursday that they were "very excited" to be able to have giant pandas return to Zoo Atlanta "after a long two years." "We've been preparing for Ping Ping and Fu Shuang's arrival. We have added many enhancements to their habitat, including new day rooms that have much more room and very top-of-the-line zoological lighting and floors and other conditions to give them the best welfare," Ferrie told Xinhua. Ping Ping, the male panda born on March 17, 2020, and Fu Shuang, the female one born on Oct. 18, 2020, departed for Zoo Atlanta from Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport in southwest China's Sichuan Province. ■

item.title: Skills on display, employment changes in motion at WorldSkills Shanghai
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
* The seven new skills making their debut at the WorldSkills Competition in Shanghai offer clues to where economic demand is heading, reflecting growth in areas ranging from the digital economy and smart manufacturing to service consumption. * Artificial intelligence is reshaping what happens inside jobs, expanding what workers are expected to do and changing the division of labor between humans and technology. * China is updating vocational programs, expanding skills training and strengthening links between schools and industry to keep talent supply in step with rapidly evolving industry demand. by Xinhua writers Ding Yinghua and Zhou Rui SHANGHAI, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- A drone assembled from scores of parts navigated its way around obstacles. A mobile robot, after programming and fine-tuning by a competitor, identified and grasped objects. In a mock store, meanwhile, another competitor arranged merchandise, served customers, and switched between in-store sales and livestreaming. Over four days at the 48th WorldSkills Competition in Shanghai, scenes involving 64 skills told a broader story of economic transformation: new technologies and shifting market needs are creating fresh demand, job roles are being reshaped, and the skills economies need are evolving with them. With all competition events completed, the global skills gathering is set to conclude with a closing ceremony on Sunday. This year's edition brought together 1,385 competitors from 68 countries and regions, while seven skills made their debuts, including unmanned aerial systems, software testing and retail. Francis Hourant, president of WorldSkills International, said trades today are not exactly the same as they were in the 1960s, adding that the competition adjusts its portfolio to stay connected with "the reality of the industry." NEW DEMAND TAKING SHAPE The seven newcomers in Shanghai offer some of the clearest clues to where economic demand is moving. In the unmanned aerial systems arena, competitors began with around 200 separate components. They had to assemble and calibrate a drone, write the code and prepare it for autonomous flight. Once airborne, this drone was expected to scan an unfamiliar environment, map obstacles and plan its own route -- with no human intervention during the flight. Beyond the competition, similar technologies are already finding their way into everyday life. In Shenzhen in south China, drones deliver takeout to smart pickup lockers, while in southwest China's Chengdu, urban logistics drones carry goods along regular low-altitude routes, and over rice fields in northeast China, agricultural drones have become part of routine farm work. Retail presented a different scene at the Shanghai event, but still reflected the same trend. Across different modules, competitors had to take on multiple roles: arranging merchandise, pitching products to customers, hosting livestreams and handling unexpected complaints. "We are not training simply a top salesperson, but an all-round retail expert," said Chen Ying, head of the expert group at the Shanghai training base for this skill. Such a combination of skills reflects a consumer market increasingly extending beyond goods toward services and experiences. In the first eight months of 2026, China's service retail sales rose 4.9 percent year on year, outpacing the 1-percent growth in goods retail sales, as demand expanded in areas including tourism, culture, sports and leisure. "Where industries develop, new occupations emerge, and WorldSkills sets up skills accordingly," said Zhang Rui, deputy director of the WorldSkills Competition China (Tianjin) Research Center. Among the seven new skills, software testing and digital interactive media design reflect the rise of the digital economy, while unmanned aerial systems and rail vehicle technology are among the skills tied to smart manufacturing and advanced equipment, Zhang explained. AI REWRITING THE JOB If changing demand helps explain why new occupations are emerging, artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping what happens inside a job. In the web technologies competition, contestants are no longer assessed simply on their ability to write code. They must analyze user needs, decide what functions a business scenario requires, complete front- and back-end development, and deliver a finished product. Wu Yingxiang, a technical expert and coach for the Chinese team in WorldSkills web technologies, said AI is making code generation much faster, thus expanding what programmers are expected to do. "Every programmer may now become a project manager and a product manager," he said. At another hall, contestants in the digital interactive media design competition moved from product planning to image processing, video production and interaction design during more than 20 hours of competition across four days. Notably, even as AI begins to take over some basic work in the industry, the training remains highly demanding. Zhou Jiaxiang, a member of China's national training squad for this skill, described a six-hour video-production module in which contestants may have to adjust dozens or even hundreds of parameters and fine-tune transition effects frame by frame. Data show that demand for AI-related skills has risen rapidly in China. Newly posted campus-recruitment positions in AI surged 47.3 percent year on year in the first five months of 2026, according to data from the talent research arm of Maimai, a Chinese networking and recruitment platform. For Hourant, this shift points to a changing division of labor rather than an either/or choice between humans and AI. "It is not AI in the end," he said, adding that the future lies in combining human skills with AI. BUILDING SKILLS FOR TOMORROW The skills on display in Shanghai point to a challenge, namely whether the supply of skilled workers can keep pace with industries that are evolving faster than before. Official data reveal that China has more than 220 million skilled workers, including over 72 million highly skilled workers. Yet gaps remain in fast-growing sectors. According to the Ministry of Education, China faced a shortage of more than 10 million highly skilled workers in areas related to the digital economy and intelligent manufacturing in 2025, making the expansion of skilled talent a top priority. The country has been stepping up efforts to reduce this shortfall. The ministry added 27 programs to the country's vocational education catalog in July, covering fields like the digital economy, AI, the low-altitude economy and advanced equipment, with new offerings related to humanoid robots, to better match talent supply with emerging and future industries. Over 5.5 million instances of subsidized vocational skills training were provided in the first half of 2026, with programs focusing on areas such as AI, advanced manufacturing, new-energy vehicles and the low-altitude economy, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security noted. Shanghai Information Technology College, for example, has added four programs tailored to the city's AI industry and brought real production scenarios, technical standards and company projects into the teaching environment. Elsewhere, schools are strengthening links with industry to keep training in step with swiftly changing industry needs. At Jiangxi Software Vocational and Technical University in east China, the campus is integrated with an industrial park, with nearly 100 companies involved in tailored training. Enterprise engineers teach classes, while real commercial projects are brought onto campus. "Vocational education cannot be run behind closed doors," said Vice Principal of Shanghai Information Technology College Sun Pengtao. "Programs have to be updated along with industry." (Video reporters: Ding Ting and Zhou Rui; Video editors: Hong Liang and Zhu Cong) ■

item.title: Asian Games | Day 8: Boonson equals Asian 200m record, Shavkatov provisionally suspended
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
by sportswriter Li Jia NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- Thailand's Puripol Boonson stormed to men's 200m gold in 19.88 seconds to equal the Asian record at the 2026 Asian Games on Sunday, while Uzbekistan's MMA bronze medalist Nodirbek Shavkatov was provisionally suspended after testing positive for meldonium. Shavkatov, 23, who won bronze in the men's modern MMA 71kg event, became the first medalist and third athlete at these Games to return a positive doping test. No decision has been announced on the status of his medal. On the track, Boonson completed an Asian Games sprint double, winning the men's 200m in 19.88 to equal the Asian record set by China's Xie Zhenye in 2019. China's Huang Youwen took silver in 20.45, while Japan's Soshi Mizukubo was third in 20.56. The 20-year-old Thai had broken the Games record with 20.10 in Saturday's semifinal before shaving another 0.22 seconds off the mark despite a slight headwind. He won the 100m on Friday in a Games-record 9.90. "It's not that different - just more adrenaline and more excitement, and I was more eager to win the gold," Boonson said of his mindset at the Games. "I'm going to aim for more golds and more records. I can't say how fast it's going to be, but there will be more records and faster times." China's 17-year-old Chen Yujie, winner of the women's 100m, took silver in the 200m in 22.93, 0.15 seconds behind Singapore's Shanti Pereira, who won in 22.78. India's Harita Bhadra was third in 23.20. Asian record holder Yan Ziyi of China won the women's javelin with a Games-record 70.46 meters on her opening attempt, while compatriot Huang Yingying took the women's long jump gold with a leap of 6.55 meters. China's Chen Yuanjiang won the men's 110m hurdles in 13.15, while Wu Yanni took bronze in the women's 100m hurdles in 13.12 behind Japan's Mako Fukube. Japan's Hayato Katsuki won the men's marathon race walk on home soil, while Kazakhstan's Yasmina Toxanbayeva took the women's title. China claimed two more table tennis golds. Huang Youzheng and Lin Shidong beat Japan's Tomokazu Harimoto and Hiroto Shinozuka 4-2 in the men's doubles final, while Wang Manyu defeated compatriot and Paris Olympic silver medalist Sun Yingsha 4-2 to win the women's singles title. China also swept the day's synchronized diving titles. Chen Yiwen and Chen Jia won the women's 3-meter springboard synchro, while Yang Hao and Lian Junjie claimed the men's 10-meter platform synchro title. In artistic swimming, China's Lin Yanjun and Xu Huiyan won the duet title after the free routine, ahead of Japan's Moe Higa and Tomoka Sato. BMX freestyle park made its Asian Games debut, with China's Sun Sibei recovering from a warm-up crash and a disappointing first run to win with 93.80 points on her second attempt. Japan's Miharu Ozawa took silver with 91.20, while China's Sun Jiaqi claimed bronze with 90.20. China also struck gold in women's street skateboarding as 15-year-old Zhu Yuanling climbed from fifth in qualifying to win with 166.57 points. Japan's Yumeka Oda earned silver with 161.96, while China's defending champion Cui Chenxi took bronze. World No. 1 Ibuki Matsumoto of Japan finished fifth. "I'd been practicing that trick in my second run for a long time, and it's one I can usually land, so I didn't feel like I needed to be that nervous," Zhu said. "It's amazing. I still feel a bit dazed. Actually I didn't expect to win gold." China took the top two places in the men's trampoline super final, with Yan Langyu winning gold with 65.09 points and Wang Zisai taking silver with 63.83. Weightlifting produced three world records as Song Kuk Hyang of the DPR Korea won the women's 69kg title. Song set a snatch world record of 121kg before lifting a world-record 152kg in the clean and jerk for a world-record total of 273kg. China took the women's 77kg gold with lifts of 118kg in the snatch and 140kg in the clean and jerk for a 258kg total. In fencing, Kirill Prokhodov helped Kazakhstan claim its first gold of the competition with a dramatic 43-42 comeback victory over South Korea in the men's epee team final. South Korea won the women's sabre team title after beating host Japan 45-31. After eight days of competition, China leads the medal table with 119 gold, 48 silver and 38 bronze medals. Japan is second with 37 gold, 61 silver and 58 bronze, while South Korea is third with 20 gold, 23 silver and 39 bronze. ■

item.title: Expo highlights China's sustained efforts to boost global digital trade cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-27
HANGZHOU, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- No steering wheel, no pedals and no rearview mirrors. For the fifth consecutive year at the Global Digital Trade Expo, Tesla once again pushed the boundaries of imagination, this time via its fully autonomous Cybercab. The two-seat Cybercab features butterfly doors and a large interactive touchscreen, relying on camera-based vision and sensors to navigate without human intervention. This futuristic vehicle was just one glimpse of the AI-driven future on display at this expo. With more than one-third of exhibitors focusing on AI, alongside the collective debut of AI application pilot bases, AI undoubtedly stole the expo's spotlight in 2026. The fifth Global Digital Trade Expo, held from Sept. 23 to 27 in Hangzhou, a tech hub in east China's Zhejiang Province, attracted over 50,000 participants from 163 countries and regions. It highlighted how AI is reshaping trade patterns and how China is dedicated to promoting global digital trade cooperation. AI, DIGITAL ECONOMY From households and industries to urban governance, the expo spotlighted emerging trends and drivers of digital trade in the AI era, accelerating the commercialization of frontier products and technologies for a wider global market. In the case of urban governance, space data and AI are seeing accelerated integration into practical scenarios. Notably, professional data intelligence provider Merit Interactive released MUMO, an urban traffic large model that fuses high-resolution satellite imagery with ground traffic data. "Traffic police can leverage the model to simulate urban green wave schemes, comparing queue lengths and traffic capacity under different scenarios to optimize signal control plans," said Fang Yi, CEO of Merit Interactive. For consumers, AI is becoming more intuitive and personal. AI-powered smart glasses provider Rokid unveiled its second-generation AI glasses at the showpiece in Hangzhou, featuring real-time navigation, instant translation and photography capabilities. "The AI assistant has evolved to understand what you need," said Ye Ziling, a staff member at the Rokid booth, noting that these new glasses support bidirectional and call translation. AI is also empowering businesses. Accio Work, an AI agent platform by tech giant Alibaba, allows enterprises to assign roles to AI, automating tasks around the clock. More than 10 million small and medium-sized enterprises worldwide now run their businesses on Accio Work. Its user count has grown more than 30-fold in a single year. "In the past, we had to outsource many services. Now, with AI, we can handle much of the work ourselves," said a businessman from Russia. "China's speed in technological innovation and application is amazing." The 2026 expo featured 170,000 square meters of exhibition space, with international exhibitors accounting for over 20 percent of the total. The number of overseas pavilions also exceeded the combined total of all previous editions. According to a guideline on boosting reform and innovative development of digital trade released in November 2024, China expects the share of digitally deliverable service trade in its total service trade to exceed 45 percent by 2029 and 50 percent by 2035. TOKEN ECONOMY A highlight of this year's expo was the debut of a token-themed zone. It drew crowds of visitors eager to understand tokens -- the basic units AI models use to process information, which have become a barometer of industry development and a key indicator of AI adoption. In the domestic market, token demand has skyrocketed, partly driven by China's "AI plus" initiative and the explosive growth of agent-based deployment. As early as March this year, national daily token calls exceeded 140 trillion, representing a more than 1,000-fold surge from 100 billion at the beginning of 2024, according to data released by the National Data Administration. From computing power infrastructure and mainstream large models like Qwen and DeepSeek to smart hardware, the token-themed zone showcased how tokens are rapidly transforming from technical metrics into tradable digital commodities. "The zone visualizes abstract AI capabilities, helping participants understand the logic of computing power trade," said Li Yang, director of the Zhejiang International Economic Expo Center, noting that while digital trade traditionally focused on software and data, token services allow computing power to be metered and traded by usage, creating a new form of digital commodity. Experts believe that by addressing core issues such as metering, pricing and management, token exports can transform China's accumulated expertise from real industrial applications into on-demand intelligent services accessible to global clients. PLATFORM FOR GLOBAL DIALOGUE Beyond being a technology showcase, the expo also serves as a crucial bridge for international dialogue and mechanism building. The China-Arab AI International Cooperation & AFDE First China-Arab Digital Dialogue, which took place during the expo this year, brought together over 200 participants from home and abroad. Seven cooperation projects worth 255 million U.S. dollars were signed, covering various areas, including robotics and smart manufacturing. China is not only a trade partner but also a helper for the next generation of digital economic development in Arab countries, said Atef Ahmed Helmy, chairman of the General Assembly at the Arab Federation for Digital Economy (AFDE). The expo this year also witnessed a dialogue on BRICS special economic zones, focusing on practical cooperation. In 2025, the number of Chinese enterprises with trade records with other BRICS members exceeded 300,000 for the first time, rising 8.8 percent year on year. Also, the China Center for Cooperation on Special Economic Zones in BRICS Countries was launched in Hangzhou last year. Ali Murtopo Simbolon, deputy minister of the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs of the Republic of Indonesia, said that this center highlights pragmatic cooperation, knowledge exchange and partnership among member states. "China started building special economic zones early with remarkable results. The zones are playing a significant role in the country's modernization," said Ge Shunqi, a professor at the Institute of Chinese Path to Modernization at Nankai University, located in north China. "At UNCTAD, we believe digital trade must be open, fair and development-oriented. This requires investment in connectivity and skills and rules that encourage innovation while protecting competition, consumers and trust," said Pedro Manuel Moreno, acting secretary-general of UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD). "We greatly value our cooperation with China and welcome the role of this expo in encouraging dialogue, partnership and practical solutions," noted Moreno. "UNCTAD stands ready to deepen this cooperation." ■

item.title: China to work with all countries to build a community with a shared future for humanity: VP
item.description:

Chinese Vice President Han Zheng delivers a speech at the general debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at the UN headquarters in New York on Sept. 26, 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei) UNITED NATIONS, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- China will join hands with all other countries to build a community with a shared future for humanity and make the world a better place for all, said Chinese Vice President Han Zheng on Saturday. Han made the remarks when delivering a speech at the general debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. The world is witnessing intertwined changes and turbulence, protracted geopolitical conflicts, widening development gaps and a growing number of global challenges, he said. Noting that Chinese President Xi Jinping put forward the Global Development Initiative at the 76th Session of the UN General Assembly, and has since then proposed the Global Security Initiative, the Global Civilization Initiative and the Global Governance Initiative, Han said these initiatives provide strategic guidance for the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. He said that more and more countries want to join hands to shoulder the historic mission of addressing difficulties and challenges, and advancing the well-being of all humanity. Han put forward four proposals: First, safeguard the postwar international order and foster lasting peace based on common security. Turn into action the vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative, and sustainable security, and reject the Cold War mindset and bloc confrontation. Settle differences and disputes through dialogue and consultation, and oppose unilateral military actions that violate the UN Charter and circumvent Security Council authorization. Second, address the global development predicament and promote prosperity for all through openness and cooperation. Keep development at the center of the international agenda, and jointly forge a global development partnership based on unity and equality and that is balanced and inclusive. Give priority to key areas including poverty reduction, food security and energy transition, step up resource input, and increase support for countries in the Global South. Take a people-centered approach, strive for the positive and for good, and make efforts to narrow the digital divide. Firmly safeguard the multilateral trading system, build an open world economy, and see that economic globalization is inclusive and delivers benefits to all. Third, advance exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations and rebuild unity and mutual trust through communication and dialogue. Use the UN platform to boost international people-to-people exchanges, promote mutual understanding and amity among all peoples and the common development of diverse civilizations. Reject ideological prejudice, and respect the development paths and social systems decided on independently by the people of all countries. Deepen the sharing of governance practices and jointly explore ways to tackle challenges facing our times. Fourth, stay committed to multilateralism and take steps to safeguard fairness and justice. China holds that all countries, big or small, are equal members of the international community, and that world affairs should be handled by all through consultation, and rule of law, fairness and justice in international affairs should be jointly upheld. Countries should join forces and act together to safeguard the UN and make it stronger. China supports the UN in reforming and improving itself, and in effectively addressing global challenges including climate change and public health security. Han pointed out that the People's Republic of China restored its lawful seat in the United Nations in 1971, which is of profound and far-reaching significance for both China and the world. Over the past 55 years, China has been a stabilizing force in times of volatility, he said, noting that China is firmly committed to pursuing peaceful development, and has the best track record on peace and security among major countries. A main engine driving common development, China has created two miracles at home, namely, fast economic growth and long-term social stability, and it has, over many years, contributed around 30 percent to global growth, Han said. He said that China, a progressive force in an era of change, has always stood up for the legitimate rights and interests of developing countries, and worked toward a more just and equitable global governance system. Han said that no matter how the international dynamics evolve, China remains unchanged in its pursuit of peace and development, in its dedication to safeguarding fairness and justice, and in its commitment to multilateralism. During his stay in New York, Han had separate meetings with Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic, Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides, Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama, and Kiribati President Taneti Maamau. The presidents spoke highly of the major ideas and initiatives proposed by Xi, expressed admiration for China's development achievements, and reaffirmed their governments' firm adherence to the one-China principle. They also expressed willingness to further enhance strategic mutual trust with China, deepen practical cooperation, strengthen multilateral coordination, and make greater contributions to the well-being of the people and global sustainable development. ■ Chinese Vice President Han Zheng delivers a speech at the general debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at the UN headquarters in New York on Sept. 26, 2026.
